Class WhoEmailLinkAutoConfiguration

java.lang.Object
org.jwcarman.who.autoconfigure.WhoEmailLinkAutoConfiguration
@AutoConfiguration(after=WhoAutoConfiguration.class, afterName="org.springframework.boot.mail.autoconfigure.MailSenderAutoConfiguration") @EnableConfigurationProperties(WhoProperties.class) @ConditionalOnClass(name="org.jwcarman.who.emaillink.EmailLinkLoginMethod") @ConditionalOnBooleanProperty(name="who.email-link.enabled", matchIfMissing=true) public class WhoEmailLinkAutoConfiguration extends Object
Turns email-link sign-in on when who-email-link is on the classpath; who.email-link.enabled=false turns it off.

Startup fails with a WhoConfigurationException when who.email-link.link-base-url or who.email-link.code-secret is missing, when who.email-link.resend-interval exceeds who.email-link.token-ttl, or when no EmailLinkSender is available.

    • emailLinkIssuer

      @Bean @ConditionalOnMissingBean public EmailLinkIssuer emailLinkIssuer(EmailCredentialService emailCredentialService, WhoService whoService, EmailLinkTokenRepository emailLinkTokenRepository, org.springframework.beans.factory.ObjectProvider<EmailLinkSender> emailLinkSender, EmailLinkSettings settings, Clock clock, WhoEventPublisher whoEventPublisher, org.springframework.beans.factory.ObjectProvider<io.micrometer.observation.ObservationRegistry> observationRegistry, org.springframework.core.io.ResourceLoader resourceLoader)

      settings - the email-link settings
      clock - stamps the token and events
      whoEventPublisher - publishes the link-issued event
      observationRegistry - observes each issue, when the application has one
      resourceLoader - checks whether Spring's mail support is on the classpath
      Returns:
      the issuer

    • whoEmailLinkExecutor

      @Bean(name="whoEmailLinkExecutor", defaultCandidate=false) @ConditionalOnMissingBean(name="whoEmailLinkExecutor") public Executor whoEmailLinkExecutor(org.springframework.beans.factory.ObjectProvider<org.springframework.core.task.TaskDecorator> taskDecorators)
      Sends sign-in emails off the request thread, so a known and an unknown address answer alike. Not a default candidate, so it never stands in for the application's own executor.

      Applies the application's TaskDecorator beans as Spring Boot does to its own executors (one on its own, several in order), so a ContextPropagatingTaskDecorator carries the request's trace and logging context to the send.

      Parameters:
      taskDecorators - the application's task decorators, in order
      Returns:
      the executor

    • emailAddressChanges

      @Bean @ConditionalOnMissingBean public EmailAddressChanges emailAddressChanges(EmailCredentialService emailCredentialService, EmailAddressRequestRepository emailAddressRequestRepository, org.springframework.beans.factory.ObjectProvider<EmailLinkSender> emailLinkSender, org.springframework.core.io.ResourceLoader resourceLoader, EmailLinkSettings settings, WhoProperties properties, Clock clock, WhoEventPublisher whoEventPublisher)
      Adds or replaces an address only once its owner confirms it, by link or code. The link goes to who.email-link.address-confirmation-url, or the sign-in link's base URL. Startup fails when there is no EmailLinkSender: no bean, and no Spring mail.
      Parameters:
      emailCredentialService - adds and revokes the addresses
      emailAddressRequestRepository - the pending changes

      settings - the email-link settings
      properties - who's properties, for the confirmation URL
      clock - stamps the request and events
      whoEventPublisher - publishes address events
      Returns:
      the address changes
